seo.title: Databricks AI Index
seo.description: The Databricks AI Index tracks enterprise AI from anonymized Unity Gateway traffic: which models companies use, where spend goes, how coding agents compare.

header.intro: **Explore the tokenomics of enterprise AI:** which models companies use, where spending goes, and which coding agents deliver the best quality for the cost. Based on aggregated, anonymized data from thousands of enterprises using [Unity Gateway](https://www.databricks.com/product/artificial-intelligence/unity-gateway).

proprietary.title: Token and wallet share by **proprietary** provider

open_source.title: Token and wallet share by **open-weight** provider

long_term.title: How enterprises **mix models** over time
long_term.intro: These charts cover a longer period but only include traffic to models hosted by Databricks, so they draw on fewer customers. Because the method differs, these numbers don't match the other charts on this page.

spend.title: What a user spends in a week

frontier.title: Cost/Quality Frontier for Coding
frontier.intro: Measured on an internal benchmark built from Unity Gateway traces of real enterprise coding tasks from the Databricks engineering organization.

scatter.title: Cost per task vs quality
scatter.description: Pass rate against average cost per task on Databricks' internal coding benchmark, one point per model. Hover over a point for exact values.
scatter.note: Built from internal benchmarks on the Databricks codebase. Anthropic models are shown in Claude Code, all other models in Codex.

quality.title: Highest quality
quality.caption: Top 10 models, ranked by highest pass rate on the coding benchmark.

time.title: Shortest time per task
time.caption: Top 10 models, ranked by shortest average time to finish a task (minutes).

cost.title: Lowest cost per task
cost.caption: Top 10 models, ranked by lowest average cost per task (USD).

token_share.title: Token share by model
token_share.description: Weekly share of Unity Gateway tokens across proprietary models.
token_share.note: Input plus output tokens routed through Unity Gateway, including traffic routed to external model providers.

wallet_share.title: Share of wallet by model
wallet_share.description: Weekly share of list-price spend across proprietary models on Unity Gateway.
wallet_share.note: Tokens priced at each provider's published list price, with cache reads at the cache-read rate. Includes traffic routed to external model providers; not what Databricks bills.

spend.title: Weekly spend per active user
spend.description: Weekly spend at list price for the median Unity Gateway user and the users at the 90th and 99th percentiles.
spend.note: Each user's input, cached and output tokens priced at each provider's published list price; human users only.

open_source_token_share.title: Token share by model
open_source_token_share.description: Weekly share of Unity Gateway tokens across open-weight models.
open_source_token_share.note: Input plus output tokens routed through Unity Gateway, including traffic routed to external model providers.

open_source_wallet_share.title: Share of wallet by model
open_source_wallet_share.description: Weekly share of list-price spend across open-weight models on Unity Gateway.
open_source_wallet_share.note: Tokens priced at each provider's published list price, with cache reads at the cache-read rate. Includes traffic routed to external model providers; not what Databricks bills.

open_weight_share.title: Open-weight share of tokens
open_weight_share.description: Weekly share of tokens on Databricks-hosted models that go to open-weight models.
open_weight_share.note: Input plus output tokens to Databricks-hosted models on Unity Gateway. Open-weight: GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, GPT-OSS and Gemma; the rest is proprietary (Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok). Traffic without a model name is excluded.

providers_used.title: Companies using multiple model providers
providers_used.description: Weekly share of active companies by how many model providers they have used on Databricks-hosted models.
providers_used.note: Among companies active each week, counts every provider a company has used since July 20, 2026, so early weeks reflect less history. Gemini and Gemma count as one provider, as do GPT and GPT-OSS.
